newsitem.title: USA: Big B board said still assessing bids.
newsitem.headline: Big B board said still assessing bids.

text.p: The board of Big B Inc. met at the company's Alabama headquarters Sunday to assess offers from interested bidders, according to a source familiar with the situation.
Big B, target of a hostile takeover by Revco D.S. Inc., had set an Oct. 25 deadline for bids from interested parties after it rejected Revco's $332 million takeover offer as inadequate.
Officials of Big B could not be reached to comment, although the company earlier indicated that bidding interest was at more than the $15 per share offered by Revco.
In addition to Revco, potential bidders cited by industry experts include Eckerd Corp.

The sale of Big B would mark the latest acquisition in the rapidly consolidating drugstore industry. Rite Aid Corp. signed an agreement this month to buy West Coast chain Thrifty PayLess Inc. for $1.4 billion and Thrift Drug Inc., a unit of J.C. Penney Co Inc., agreed in August to buy Fay's Inc. for about $285 million.
Big B's stock has been trading at about $16 per share on the Nasdaq market on views that the company will be sold for more than Revco's $15 per share offer.
The Bessemer, Ala.-based chain has been hurt by deteriorating profit margins and sales and its earnings have disappointed Wall Street.
Like many other regional drugstore chains, Big B is fighting problems that have accompanied the burgeoning clout of managed health care companies and huge discount retailers.
